excerpt: Compare buying and renting in Dubai over your intended stay, including transaction costs, annual expenses, flexibility and the use of your capital.
introduction:
Buying can offer control over a Dubai home and an asset to sell later; renting can preserve flexibility and avoid the buyer's upfront transaction costs. Neither choice is automatically cheaper. The result depends on your planned stay, the actual home, future sale price, financing and what your money could otherwise earn.

Compare both choices over the same period and include costs that are easy to overlook. The worked calculation in this guide explains the method using one consistent set of example inputs.
takeaways: Use the same home standard, period and cash-flow assumptions for the buying and renting options.
Include purchase and sale costs, owner expenses and the possible change in property value.
Consider the return on capital tied up in a purchase, financing risk and the value of flexibility.

sections.heading: What should the comparison include?
sections.body:
For buying, start with the purchase price, registration and brokerage, bank costs if relevant, annual service charges, insurance and maintenance. At the end of the period, deduct the assumed sale price and include selling costs and the remaining mortgage if one exists. The result is sensitive to the sale assumption.

For renting, include rent, expected renewal changes, non-refundable lease and agency charges, utilities not paid under the ownership scenario and moving costs. Treat refundable deposits as a cash requirement and record any actual deduction separately. Use comparable properties rather than comparing a small rental with a much larger purchase.

The [JVC and Arjan area guide](/journal/jvc-vs-arjan-apartment-investment-comparison) helps assess location and building differences. Verify current offers and personal requirements for the specific home.

sections.heading: A simplified five-year example
sections.body:
Suppose a buyer pays AED 1,200,000 cash, plus AED 60,000 acquisition costs. Assume owner costs of AED 15,000 a year for five years, selling costs of AED 30,000 and a sale for the same AED 1,200,000. The simplified ownership cost is AED 165,000: acquisition costs plus AED 75,000 owner costs plus selling costs.

Suppose a comparable rental costs AED 85,000 a year for five years with no change, totalling AED 425,000. These example inputs show how each cost contributes to the overall comparison. The chart shows the narrow totals before tenant fees, moving expenses, tax, financing and the return that could have been earned on capital.

The sale price is uncertain. If it is AED 200,000 lower, the simplified ownership cost becomes AED 365,000 under the same other assumptions; if higher, it falls. A real comparison must also account for the different timing of all cash flows.

sections.heading: Account for the capital and payment timing
sections.body:
The buyer in the example ties up AED 1,260,000 at the start, while the renter may retain capital and pay rent over time. Estimate the after-cost return that could reasonably be earned on available cash and model the timing on both sides. This is an opportunity-cost assumption, not a guaranteed investment return.

With a mortgage, replace the cash purchase with the actual down payment, bank charges, monthly payments and remaining loan balance at sale. Separate interest from principal: principal repayments affect the remaining debt and sale proceeds, while interest is a financing cost. A variable rate or refinancing can change the result.

Use a spreadsheet or qualified adviser for a discounted cash-flow comparison if the decision is material. Avoid adding a guessed return to only one side while ignoring when the other side's payments occur.

sections.heading: Check the transaction and lease terms
sections.body:
DLD's [property sale registration page](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/eservices/property-sale-registration/) lists the official completed-property process and fees, including 2% of the sale value for each party in its stated schedule. The agreement can allocate costs differently; request a current quote. The [upfront Dubai buying cost guide](/journal/total-upfront-cost-of-buying-property-in-dubai) explains the components.

For a rental, check the lease, payment dates, deposit, maintenance and early-exit provisions. DLD's [Ejari service](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/eservices/register-renew-ejari-contract/) describes tenancy registration; confirm the current process and charges for your contract. Keep written evidence rather than relying on an assumed renewal or fee.

For either option, inspect the actual home and confirm what is included in the price or rent.

sections.heading: Match the decision to your plans
sections.body:
A short or uncertain stay may make the cost and time of buying and selling more important. A longer stay gives more time over which to spread one-off transaction costs, but it does not guarantee that the home will rise in value. Renting can also involve moving costs and changes in rent or availability.

Test a range of sale prices, rent renewals, interest rates and length of stay. Keep an emergency reserve and consider how a job change or family need would affect the decision. The right answer is the one that fits your finances and required flexibility under more than one plausible scenario.

If you intend to buy, verify the ownership right and relevant documents for the exact property. Obtain independent financial or legal advice where appropriate.

sections.heading: Consider the practical trade-offs
sections.body:
Ownership may allow you to make permitted changes to a home, but check building approvals and the cost of work. A tenant should ask the landlord which changes are allowed and whether the property must be restored at the end of the lease. In both cases, building rules and the actual agreement matter.

Think about the time needed for a future move. Selling may require viewings, negotiations and clearance, while a tenancy may involve notice periods and early-exit conditions. Put a value on the flexibility your household needs without treating it as a fixed market price.

sections.heading: Explore current homes
sections.body: Browse the [Aliyas Dubai project collection](/projects?emirate=Dubai) and ask for current purchase or rental options matching your requirements. [Contact Aliyas](/contact) with your preferred location, intended stay and total budget. Request written terms and compare them with your own cash-flow assumptions before committing.
